summary: The module implements a Variational Inference engine with support for Mean-Field and Full-Covariance Gaussian families. However, it contains critical defects in the gradient computation for the entropy term (which will cause variance collapse) and broken convenience functions due to a mismatch between standard and traced arithmetic operations.

critical.title: Incorrect Entropy Gradient (Variance Collapse)
critical.description: The implementation computes the gradient of -log q(z; phi) treating z as a constant (fixed value) rather than a reparameterized function of phi (Line 422: `map traced-value t-z`).
critical.impact: For log-sigma, the gradient of -log q(z_fixed) has an expectation of 0 (since E[epsilon^2] = 1). The correct gradient (using analytical entropy or fully reparameterized path) should be +1 (pushing sigma to increase). The model effectively lacks an entropy term in the gradient. It will behave like Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation, likely causing the variance sigma^2 to collapse to zero (overfitting), rather than converging to the true posterior variance.
critical.mathematical_detail: The ELBO gradient should include d/d(log_sigma) H[q] = +1 for each dimension. By detaching z when computing log q, this term evaluates to E[epsilon^2 - 1] = 0 instead.
critical.recommendation: Replace the Monte Carlo estimation of the entropy term with the analytical entropy gradient (since mf-gaussian-entropy is available), or fix the reparameterization by not detaching z: calculate log-q using t-z directly (requires traced-log-normal-pdf to handle traced z).

critical.title: Broken Convenience Functions (Runtime Crash)
critical.description: vi-fit-linear-regression defines log-joint using standard Scheme operators (+, *, log-normal-pdf). It passes this to vi-fit, which passes it to vi-step-adam -> elbo-gradient-mf. elbo-gradient-mf calls this function with traced objects (from core/autodiff/reverse-diff.ss). Since standard operators in prelude.ss are not overloaded to handle traced objects (and traced-add etc. must be used), this will cause a runtime type error.
critical.impact: Calling vi-fit-linear-regression will cause a runtime crash when the gradient computation attempts to use standard arithmetic on traced values.
critical.recommendation: Rewrite vi-fit-linear-regression to use vi-fit-traced and provide both a standard log-joint (for ELBO estimation) and a traced-log-joint (for gradient computation using traced-add, traced-mul, etc.).

high.title: Full Gaussian Cholesky Diagonal Not Constrained
high.description: The Cholesky factor L is constructed directly from unconstrained flat parameters. The diagonal elements are not constrained to be positive.
high.impact: If optimization drives a diagonal element to be negative, log-det (Line 247) will fail or return NaN. Mean-field Gaussian avoids this by optimizing log-stds.
high.recommendation: Parameterize the diagonal of the Cholesky factor using exp or softplus to ensure positivity. Store log-diagonal elements and exponentiate during reconstruction.

medium.title: API Consistency Issue: vi-fit vs vi-fit-traced
medium.description: vi-fit implies a single log-joint function is sufficient. This forces the user to write their model using traced-* operators (e.g., traced-add), which is leaky abstraction and makes the function slower/unusable for simple debugging with numbers.
medium.recommendation: Deprecate vi-fit or make it explicitly require the user to provide two functions (as vi-fit-traced does). Alternatively, implement trace-lift to automatically convert standard functions to traced versions.

medium.title: Division Safety in ELBO Estimation
medium.description: The ELBO estimate divides by K without checking if K is zero.
medium.impact: Calling elbo-estimate with K=0 will cause a division by zero error.
medium.recommendation: Add guard: (if (= K 0) (error 'elbo-estimate "K must be positive") ...)

low.title: Magic Numbers for Pi
low.description: Pi is hardcoded as 3.141592653589793 in multiple locations.
low.recommendation: Define (define pi 3.141592653589793) once and reference it throughout, or use (acos -1) for maximum precision.

low.title: Redundant take/drop Definitions
low.description: Local definitions of take/drop may shadow or conflict with prelude definitions. take-traced and drop-traced are identical to take/drop but with different names.
low.recommendation: Use the prelude versions if available, or consolidate these utilities.

missing: Posterior variance convergence (would expose variance collapse bug)
Gradient correctness validation against numerical differentiation
recommendations: Add test that specifically asserts posterior variance matches expected value for normal-normal conjugate model
Add test for vi-fit-linear-regression with simple known-answer case
Add numerical gradient check for ELBO gradient (compare analytical vs finite differences)
Add edge case tests for empty lists and boundary values

elbo_formulation.notes: ELBO = E_q[log p(x,z)] - E_q[log q(z)] = E_q[log p(x,z)] + H[q] is correctly stated in comments and elbo-with-entropy implementation.

reparameterization_trick.notes: z = mu + sigma * epsilon correctly implemented for mean-field Gaussian. Full Gaussian z = mu + L*epsilon also correct.

gradient_computation.notes: The gradient of -log q(z; phi) detaches z from the computation graph, effectively removing the entropy gradient. This causes the optimizer to ignore the entropy term, leading to variance collapse.

log_probability.notes: mf-gaussian-log-prob uses log-normal-pdf from bayesian.ss. full-gaussian-log-prob implements Mahalanobis distance via forward solve correctly, but log_det term requires positive diagonals.

entropy.notes: H[N(mu, diag(sigma^2))] = sum of 0.5*(1 + log(2*pi*sigma_i^2)) correctly implemented for mean-field. Full Gaussian entropy also correct.

issues.issue: log of potentially negative diagonal elements
Uses 1e-8 epsilon for numerical stability - good practice
Proper epsilon (1e-8) used in Adam denominator

good_practices: Log-space parameterization for mean-field std deviations (log-stds)
Adam optimizer epsilon for numerical stability
Use of log-probabilities throughout to avoid underflow

strengths: Generic vfamily-* interface allows extension to new variational families
case-lambda for optional arguments with sensible defaults
weaknesses: Confusing dual API (vi-fit vs vi-fit-traced) with non-obvious requirements
vi-fit misleadingly accepts standard functions but requires traced functions
No validation/error messages for incorrect function signatures
